clue.text: Turn it up intermittently — speed gives notable success

indicators.note: intermittently means taking only every other letter of the words Turn it up, starting with the first

parts.note: MPH, miles per hour, is a measure of speed

explanation.surface: A driver cranking up the pace in fits and starts and winning a famous victory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intermittently' keeps the 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th letters of TURNITUP, giving TRIU.
explanation.definitionFit: A triumph is a great victory or achievement, a synonym of notable success.

clue.text: One's heart is in touch for a spell

indicators.note: is in means the middle letter sits inside the other word

parts.note: a trace is a touch, a tiny amount

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letter

explanation.surface: Someone's heart is touched by a spell of romance.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of ONE is N.
explanation.definitionFit: A trance is a dazed, hypnotic state, as cast by a spell.

clue.text: Forces smile awkwardly absorbing pressure

indicators.note: absorbing means soaking up, so the shuffled letters take in the pressure letter
awkwardly means clumsily, out of order, so the letters of smile are rearranged

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Someone is made to smile awkwardly under pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to drive or push someone to act, so it forces them.

clue.text: Delivery vehicles exploit aids for anglers

parts.note: to milk is to exploit for gain
floats are bobbers that hold a fishing line up in the water

explanation.surface: Delivery vans take advantage of fishing tackle.
explanation.definitionFit: These are small electric vans used in Britain to deliver bottled milk to homes.

clue.text: Classic poet's house on the sea in France

indicators.note: on means placed next to, so the house letters sit before the French sea

parts.note: mer is French for sea

explanation.surface: A classical poet has a seaside house in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer was the ancient Greek author of the Iliad and the Odyssey.

clue.text: Analysed a test-market stocking drugs

indicators.note: stocking means holding goods inside, so the words Analysed a test-market keep a run of letters within them

explanation.surface: A trial launch has been examined, apparently in a shop that carries pharmaceuticals.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'Analysed' through 'a' into 'test'. 'drugs' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To drug someone is to calm or knock them out with medication, a synonym of the verb in the definition.

clue.text: Artistic city's redesigned around tip

indicators.note: around means the shuffled letters go round the other word
redesigned means given a new layout, so the letters of city's are rearranged

parts.note: to list is to tip or lean over, as a ship does

explanation.surface: A city's arts quarter has been redeveloped around a landfill site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip' looks like rubbish dump or advice, but it is the verb LIST, to lean.
explanation.definitionFit: Stylistic means relating to style, as artistic means relating to art.

clue.text: Benefit of lies oddly underpinning party

indicators.note: underpinning means supporting from below, so in this down clue the picked letters go beneath

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: oddly means take the odd-numbered letters of lies, first and third

explanation.surface: A political party's welfare policy rests on a pack of lies.
explanation.definitionFit: The dole is British slang for unemployment benefit.

clue.text: Vet finally has joint settlement

indicators.note: finally means take the last letter of Vet

parts.note: to own is to have
the hip is a joint

explanation.surface: A vet at last owns a share of a smallholding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' looks like an adjective with settlement, but it is the hip.
explanation.definitionFit: A township is a small town or settlement, especially in South Africa.

clue.text: Plan great changes in animal enclosure

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the enclosure

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs

indicators.note: changes means the letters of great are altered in order

explanation.surface: A scheme for big alterations to a zoo pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A strategy is a plan of action designed to achieve a goal.

clue.text: Shock a friend welcoming pressure

indicators.note: welcoming means taking a guest in, so the word for friend holds the pressure letter inside

parts.note: a pal is a friend
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Someone is shocked when a friend greets them under strain.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal is to horrify or dismay, a synonym of shock as a verb.

clue.text: Prime Minister needs best sort of growth

parts.note: Theresa May was a British Prime Minister
the flower of something is its finest part, as in the flower of youth

explanation.surface: A politician needs the finest kind of economic expansion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'growth' suggests economics, but here it is a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayflower is hawthorn blossom, a kind of plant growth that blooms in spring.

clue.text: Newly-developed African oil state

indicators.note: newly developed means something has been made over afresh, so the letters of African oil are rearranged

explanation.surface: A new oil producer has emerged in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a US state on the Pacific coast.

clue.text: Discreet attention seeker?

parts.note: not a person but the quiet hissing sound made to catch someone's eye without others noticing

explanation.surface: A shy person who wants to be noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: This whispered interjection quietly attracts someone's notice, a discreet bid for attention.

clue.text: Junior to enter grovelling initially suffering

parts.note: under means junior, lower in rank
to go in is to enter

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of grovelling

explanation.surface: A junior entering while grovelling is in for a hard time.
explanation.definitionFit: Undergoing means experiencing or enduring something, so suffering it.

clue.text: Aching to incorporate seating area, getting established

indicators.note: to incorporate means to take something into a body, so one word holds the other inside

parts.note: aching for something is longing for it
a stand is a seating area at a sports ground

explanation.surface: A stadium yearns to add a new stand and become well established.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-standing means having existed for a long time, so well established.

clue.text: Papal gag or rein, after a fashion

indicators.note: after a fashion means in some rough form, so the letters of gag or rein are reworked

explanation.surface: A pope chooses between gagging and restraining someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Gregorian refers to Pope Gregory, as in the Gregorian chant or calendar, so it is papal.

clue.text: Traders possibly accepting nothing for such a vehicle

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the shuffled letters hold the round letter
possibly means in some other possible order, so the letters of Traders are rearranged

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Dealers might take nothing in exchange for this car.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadster is an open two-seater sports car, a kind of vehicle the traders might sell.

clue.text: Insist, and offer to keep deadlock

indicators.note: to keep means to hold within, so the letters are held inside the words Insist, and offer

explanation.surface: Negotiators insist and make an offer just to keep the impasse going.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'Insist' through 'and' into 'offer'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-off is a situation where neither side can win, a stalemate.

clue.text: Extended prison term in exposed environment?

indicators.note: environment means surroundings, so the word for exposed surrounds the prison term

parts.note: outed means exposed, revealed publicly
a stretch is slang for a prison sentence

explanation.surface: A prisoner's sentence has been lengthened in some revealing setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word; 'environment' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Outstretched means stretched out or extended, as of an arm.

clue.text: Rest of page in red is redrafted

indicators.note: in places the page letter inside the shuffled letters
redrafted means written out anew, so the letters of red is are rearranged

explanation.surface: The remainder of a page in red ink has been rewritten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rest' is not remainder: a spider is a snooker rest, a cue support with long legs.
explanation.definitionFit: In snooker, a spider is a raised rest for the cue over another ball.

clue.text: Announce the lady's mistreated lad

parts.note: her means belonging to the lady

indicators.note: mistreated means badly handled, so the letters of lad are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman publicly reveals that her boy has been abused.
explanation.definitionFit: To herald is to proclaim or announce, as a royal messenger did.

clue.text: European article adopted in case of dispute

indicators.note: adopted in means taken into a family, so the article goes inside
the case of a word is its outside letters, its first and last

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A European in a legal row over a newspaper piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of dispute' gives DE, its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dane is a person from Denmark, so a European.

clue.text: Cooking, get poetic about a dish

indicators.note: about means around, so the shuffled letters go around the letter a
cooking means mixing up and transforming ingredients, so the letters of get poetic are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook turns lyrical about a favourite dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooking' shuffles GETPOETIC; 'about' puts it round A.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a British dish of minced meat topped with mashed potato, baked in an oven.

clue.text: Bought on the way up when seeing such garments

indicators.note: on the way up means rising, so in this down clue the word for bought is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: got means acquired or bought
as means when, as in 'as I arrived'

explanation.surface: Someone buys robes on a trip uphill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the way up' turns GOT into TOG. 'such garments' points back to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Togas were loose outer robes worn by citizens of ancient Rome.

clue.text: Part of problem in ironing dress

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A snag with pressing a dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A mini is a short skirt or dress ending well above the knee.

clue.text: Adulterous couple should confront this regularly ignored dynasty

parts.note: a couple is two

indicators.note: regularly ignored means every other letter of this is skipped, leaving the first and third

parts.note: the Ming dynasty ruled China from 1368 to 1644

explanation.surface: A pair should face up to this neglected family line.
explanation.definitionFit: Two-timing describes being unfaithful to a partner by seeing someone else, so adulterous.

clue.text: Country home needing assistance to make a comeback

parts.note: in means at home

parts.note: aid is assistance

explanation.surface: A household needs help to recover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make a comeback' turns AID into DIA.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a large South Asian nation.

clue.text: Hooligan sport enthusiast embracing Formula One

parts.note: RU is rugby union

indicators.note: embracing means holding in the arms, so the enthusiast surrounds the other letters

parts.note: a fan is an enthusiast
F is the abbreviation for formula
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A rowdy motorsport fan who loves Formula One.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruffian is a violent, lawless person, a synonym of hooligan.

clue.text: Argued violently after son gets sweet

indicators.note: after places the shuffled letters behind the son's letter
violently means in a wild, disordered way, so the letters of Argued are rearranged

explanation.surface: A row breaks out after a boy gets hold of some sweets.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugared means coated or sweetened with sugar, hence sweet.
